en: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, my father and Muhammad ibn Bishr al-'Abdi narrated to us, from Isma'il, who said: I said to 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, "Did the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) give glad tidings to Khadijah of a palace in Paradise?" He said: "Yes, he gave her glad tidings of a palace in Paradise made of reeds, wherein there is neither clamor nor toil."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb, and Ibn Numayr narrated to us—they said: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from 'Umarah, from Abu Zur'ah, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah saying: Gabriel came to the Prophet (pbuh) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, here is Khadijah coming to you with a vessel containing condiment, or food, or drink. So when she comes to you, convey salam to her from her Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and from me, and give her the glad tidings of a palace in Paradise made of reeds, wherein there is neither clamor nor toil." Abu Bakr said in his narration from Abu Hurayrah: and he did not say "I heard"; nor did he say in the hadith "and from me."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb both narrated to us—they said: Waki' narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us—all of them from Shu'bah; (H) and 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us—and the wording is his—my father narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Murrah, from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "Many among men attained perfection, but none among women attained perfection except Maryam bint 'Imran and Asiyah the wife of Pharaoh. And indeed, the superiority of 'A'ishah over other women is like the superiority of tharid over all other food."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Numayr and Abu Usamah narrated to us; (H) and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Usamah, Ibn Numayr, Waki', and Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, 'Abdah ibn Sulayman informed us—all of them from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, and the wording is that of the hadith of Abu Usamah; (H) and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, who said: I heard 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far saying: I heard 'Ali in Kufa saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) saying: "The best of its women is Maryam bint 'Imran, and the best of its women is Khadijah bint Khuwaylid." Abu Kurayb said: And Waki' pointed to the heaven and the earth.

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us, Mahdi ibn Maymun narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'qub narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'd, freed slave of al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far, who said: One day the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) seated me behind him on his mount, and whispered a secret to me that I will never tell to anyone among mankind.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from 'Asim, Muwarriq narrated to me, 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to me, who said: Whenever the Prophet (pbuh) returned from a journey, we would be brought out to meet him. He said: So I was brought out to meet him along with al-Hasan or al-Husayn. He said: So he carried one of us in front of him and the other behind him until we entered Medina.

Yahya ibn Yahya and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us—and the wording is Yahya's—Abu Bakr said: narrated to us, and Yahya said: Abu Mu'awiyah informed us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Muwarriq al-'Ijli, from 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far, who said: Whenever the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) returned from a journey, the children of his household would be brought out to meet him. He said: And he returned from a journey and I was rushed ahead to him, so he carried me in front of him. Then one of the two sons of Fatimah was brought, and he seated him behind him. He said: So we entered Medina, three upon a single mount.
Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu Usamah informed us, from Habib ibn al-Shahid, with the like of the hadith of Ibn 'Ulayyah and his chain of narration.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Isma'il Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Habib ibn al-Shahid, from 'Abdullah ibn Mulaykah, that 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far said to Ibn al-Zubayr: "Do you remember when we met the Messenger of Allah (pbuh)—I, you, and Ibn 'Abbas?" He said: "Yes, and he carried us and left you."

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from 'Umar—meaning Ibn Hamzah—from Salim, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said while upon the pulpit: "If you criticize his leadership"—meaning Usamah ibn Zayd—"you had already criticized the leadership of his father before him. And by Allah, he was truly worthy of it, and by Allah, he was indeed the most beloved of people to me. And by Allah, this one is truly worthy of it"—meaning Usamah ibn Zayd—"and by Allah, he is indeed among the most beloved of them to me after him; so I enjoin you to treat him well, for he is from among your righteous ones."

Yahya ibn Yahya, Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us—Yahya ibn Yahya said: informed us, and the others said: narrated to us—Isma'il—meaning Ibn Ja'far—from 'Abdullah ibn Dinar, that he heard Ibn 'Umar saying: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) dispatched an expedition and appointed Usamah ibn Zayd as commander over them. Some people criticized his leadership, so the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) stood up and said: "If you criticize his leadership, you had already criticized the leadership of his father before. And by Allah, he was truly worthy of leadership, and he was indeed among the most beloved of people to me, and this one is surely among the most beloved of people to me after him."
Ahmad ibn Sa'id al-Darimi narrated to me, Habban narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Musa ibn 'Uqbah narrated to us, Salim narrated to me, from 'Abdullah, the like of it.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Qari narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Salim ibn 'Abdullah, from his father, who used to say: We never used to call Zayd ibn Harithah anything except Zayd ibn Muhammad until the Quran revealed: "Call them by the names of their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah." Shaykh Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn 'Isa said: Abu al-'Abbas al-Sarraj and Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Yusuf al-Duwayri both informed us, saying: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us this hadith.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Bakr's—they said: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Zakariyya', from Mus'ab ibn Shaybah, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah, who said: 'A'ishah said: The Prophet (pbuh) went out one morning wearing an embroidered cloak made of black hair. Then al-Hasan ibn 'Ali came, and he took him under it; then al-Husayn came and entered with him; then Fatimah came and he took her under it; then 'Ali came and he took him under it. Then he recited: "Allah only intends to remove from you all impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you completely."

Abdullah ibn al-Rumi al-Yamami and 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-'Azim al-'Anbari both narrated to me—they said: al-Nadr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, 'Ikrimah—and he is Ibn 'Ammar—narrated to us, Iyas narrated to us, from his father, who said: I led the grey mule of the Prophet of Allah (pbuh) carrying the Prophet of Allah (pbuh), al-Hasan, and al-Husayn until I brought them into the apartment of the Prophet (pbuh)—one of them before him and the other behind him.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' narrated to us—Ibn Nafi' said: Ghundar narrated to us—Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Adi—and he is Ibn Thabit—from al-Bara', who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) having placed al-Hasan ibn 'Ali upon his shoulder while saying: "O Allah, indeed I love him, so love him."

Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Adi—and he is Ibn Thabit—al-Bara' ibn 'Azib narrated to us, who said: I saw al-Hasan ibn 'Ali upon the shoulder of the Prophet (pbuh) while he was saying: "O Allah, indeed I love him, so love him."

Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Yazid, from Nafi' ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I went out with the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) during a portion of the daytime, he not speaking to me and I not speaking to him, until he reached the marketplace of Banu Qaynuqa'. Then he returned until he reached the tent of Fatimah and said: "Is the little one there? Is the little one there?"—meaning Hasan. We thought that his mother was only detaining him to bathe him and put a necklace of beads on him. It was not long before he came running until each of them embraced his companion, and the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "O Allah, indeed I love him, so love him, and love whoever loves him."

Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to me, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Yazid narrated to me, from Nafi' ibn Jubayr, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (pbuh), that he said to Hasan: "O Allah, indeed I love him, so love him, and love whoever loves him."
Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu Dawud al-Hafari informed us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, with this chain of narration, similarly.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, he said: I heard Abu Ishaq narrating from Silah ibn Zufar, from Hudhayfah, who said: The people of Najran came to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, send to us a trustworthy man." He said: "I will certainly send to you a trustworthy man, truly trustworthy, truly trustworthy." He said: So the people craned their necks for it. He said: And he sent Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah.

Amr al-Naqid narrated to me, 'Affan narrated to us, Hammad—and he is Ibn Salamah—narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, that the people of Yemen came to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) and said: "Send with us a man to teach us the Sunnah and Islam." He said: So he took the hand of Abu 'Ubaydah and said: "This is the trustworthy man of this nation."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Isma'il Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Khalid; (H) and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, Isma'il Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, Khalid informed us, from Abu Qilabah, he said: Anas said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "Indeed, every nation has a trustworthy guardian, and indeed our trustworthy guardian, O this nation, is Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah."

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, Isma'il narrated to us, from al-Bahi, from 'Urwah, who said: 'A'ishah said to me: "Your two fathers were among those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after injury had afflicted them."
And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, with this chain of narration, and he added: meaning Abu Bakr and al-Zubayr.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Ibn Numayr and 'Abdah both narrated to us—they said: Hisham narrated to us, from his father, who said: 'A'ishah said to me: "By Allah, your two fathers were among those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after injury had afflicted them."

Ubaydullah ibn Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Khunays and Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Azdi both narrated to us—they said: Isma'il ibn Abi Uways narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) was upon Mount Hira' and it shook. The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "Be still, Hira', for there is none upon you except a prophet, or a steadfast affirmer of truth, or a martyr." And upon it were the Prophet (pbuh), Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, Talhah, al-Zubayr, and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with them).

And Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning Ibn Muhammad—narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) was upon Hira'—he, Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, Talhah, and al-Zubayr—and the rock shook. The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "Be calm, for there is none upon you except a prophet, or a steadfast affirmer of truth, or a martyr."

And Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: On the day of the Trench, 'Umar ibn Abi Salamah and I were in the fortress in which the women were—meaning the women of the Prophet (pbuh)... and he related the hadith with the meaning of the hadith of Ibn Mushir in this chain of narration, and he did not mention 'Abdullah ibn 'Urwah in the hadith, but incorporated the story into the hadith of Hisham from his father from Ibn al-Zubayr.

Isma'il ibn al-Khalil and Suwayd ibn Sa'id both narrated to us from Ibn Mushir—Isma'il said: 'Ali ibn Mushir informed us—from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: 'Umar ibn Abi Salamah and I were on the day of the Trench with the women in the fortress of Hassan. He would bend down for me at times so that I could look, and I would bend down for him at times so that he could look. I recognized my father whenever he passed on his horse bearing arms towards Banu Qurayzah. He said: And 'Abdullah ibn 'Urwah informed me from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: I mentioned that to my father, and he said: "Did you really see me, my son?" I said, "Yes." He said: "By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) combined both his parents for me on that day, saying: 'May my father and mother be ransomed for you!'"
